pin_limitation: The immutable raw file was obtained and hashed; the gist HEAD API failed. Do not relabel the raw-file revision as a verified gist HEAD.
source_license: No explicit license declaration in the inspected pinned file; attribution does not imply a license grant.
status: Implemented; actual pass/fail counts and measured diagnostics come from central TRX artifacts.

reference_tiers.description: Independent NumPy implementation of the matrix forward pass, analytic derivatives and Adam. The same NumSharp parameter buffers are exported zero-copy; the reference computes independently. Logits, loss, every gradient, updated weights and both Adam moments use exact dtype/shape/byte assertions. NumPy is not the original source implementation: the original is scalar Python.
reference_tiers.runtime: NumPy 2.4.2, CPython 3.12.12 for the initial reference execution; final runtime records are in verification artifacts.

reference_tiers.description: Separately expressed scalar-list causal forward equations, with explicit sequential summation and prefix key/value history like the source Value graph. Compared numerically, not claimed byte-identical to matrix BLAS/reductions. Analytic gradients also undergo exhaustive finite-difference checking.

KarpathyOriginalSource.Load embeds and SHA256-verifies the original microgpt.py, AST-selects its unmodified Value/linear/softmax/rmsnorm/gpt definitions, and executes three actual Value-graph backward/Adam steps plus twenty autoregressive samples. Shared starting parameter bytes; small local documents; declared shared NumPy uniform stream for sampling.
reference_tiers.claim: Numerical scalar-source parity, NOT scalar-source bit identity. Separate NumPy ledger retains exact bytes.

assertions: Vocabulary sorted by Unicode code point, with a single shared BOS/end token
Encode/decode round trip including a supplementary Unicode character
Unknown tokens and invalid context lengths rejected
Long documents are truncated at the configured block size
limits: The caller supplies documents; no file download or hidden corpus normalization is claimed.

assertions: Default one layer, width 16, four heads and context 16
27-token configuration has 4192 parameters across nine matrices
Model parameters and optimizer storage remain valid after a surrounding temporary scope closes
Forward/backward covers original width/head configuration and an additional two-layer configuration
limits: Initialization has the source's Gaussian standard deviation .08 but uses NumPy RandomState, not Python random.gauss. No identical source RNG state is asserted.

assertions: Token plus position embedding followed by the initial RMSNorm and the separate pre-attention RMSNorm
All Q/K/V projections, four causal attention heads, output projection and residual
Pre-MLP RMSNorm, 4x expansion, ReLU, contraction and residual, with no biases or final normalization
All logits are checked against independent NumPy; scalar-list equations are checked at their separate stated tolerance
Changing future tokens cannot change earlier logits
limits: Full-sequence masked matrix attention replaces incremental scalar computation. Prefix recomputation during inference replaces the source key/value cache; this is an efficiency difference, not a missing causal operation.

assertions: Every parameter gradient, including repeated-token embedding scatter and position embedding gradients, is compared with independent NumPy analytic derivatives
Every element of the 228-parameter small model is perturbed in both directions with delta=1e-5
Finite-difference error abs(numeric-analytic)/(1+abs(numeric)+abs(analytic)) must remain below 2e-6
Loss and all output logits are also checked
limits: A general-purpose scalar Value autograd API is not ported. Its complete transformer chain rule is implemented manually at matrix level, including all attention/softmax/RMSNorm/residual/MLP derivatives.

assertions: Source beta1=.85, beta2=.99, epsilon=1e-8, both bias corrections and linear learning-rate decay
Every weight and both moment buffers compare byte-for-byte after each of four independent NumPy updates
The actual training path updates every parameter and advances the optimizer step counter
limits: Adam is used, not a surrogate optimizer or frozen-weight forward-only demonstration.

assertions: Both a 200-update diagnostic and the original default 1000-update schedule genuinely train on ten embedded local names at the original architecture dimensions
All per-step losses finite, every default step callback observed, optimizer step count 1000, full-corpus post-training loss below 75 percent of pre-training loss
Independent NumPy pre-execution observed full-corpus loss 2.649477742973952 to .5453333686931137 on the 200-update fixture
Local fixture vocabulary 13, parameter count 3744
Demo uses the original 1000-update count followed by twenty generated samples
limits: The source's remotely downloaded names.txt, shuffled document order and Python RNG stream are not reproduced
No claim is made about the loss curve or generated names of the original full downloaded corpus

assertions: Twenty actual autoregressive samples at temperature .5 with context cap 16 and BOS termination
Samples contain only vocabulary characters and are reproducible for the supplied seed
An independently executed NumPy sampling loop over the same trained parameter buffers must produce the same twenty token sequences
Inference consumes trained logits rather than a canned list of names
limits: Categorical inverse-CDF sampling uses NumPy RandomState instead of Python random.choices. Exact generated strings are compared within that explicitly specified RNG contract, not against nonexistent original sample-output fixtures.

assertions: Actual original scalar-autograd loss.backward executes at all three updates
Every loss/logit/parameter gradient, updated weight and Adam moment compared at each update
Twenty samples from original incremental-key/value computation match the port
Full maximum absolute state difference is recorded in TRX
limits: Original scalar graph and vectorized reduction order differ; explicit rtol1e-9/atol1e-11 value gate, not a byte fallback
Explicit small model/documents and shared NumPy sampling stream; no original remote corpus/Python RNG equivalence

assertions: Six alternating-document updates with228 dtype/shape/byte checkpoints
Every loss/logit/allninegradientarrays and eachupdatedweight/firstmoment/secondmoment match before moving to next update
Python evolves independent parameter copies after one initial shared-buffer export
limits: Exact NumPy matrix formulation; not a scalar Python byte claim

exclusions.reason: No input.txt, urllib download, external dataset or file side effect. Callers supply local names; the demo uses a committed in-code fixture.

Matrix BLAS/reduction order and manually accumulated derivatives need not equal the original scalar Value graph bit-for-bit. Independent NumPy byte tests and scalar-equation value/finite-difference tests are separate contracts.

Original random.shuffle/gauss/choices streams and the full remote dataset are not reproduced; there are no fixed original numerical outputs to invent. Model, loss, optimizer and sampling algorithms are fully implemented.
